Lessons.Title: Solve Multiplicative Comparison Problems with Large Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will extend your understanding of multiplicative comparison to situations that involve larger quantities and larger multipliers.
In previous lessons, you interpreted discrete diagrams in which each section represented one item and used them to solve multiplicative comparison problems. You also represented multiplicative comparison situations in which different parts of the problem were unknown. In this lesson, you extend your understanding of multiplicative comparison, including ways to represent it, to include comparisons with larger amounts and multipliers.
Core relationship: Large-number multiplicative comparisons. Interpret 'times as many' with multiplication even when the base or total exceeds 100.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Notice and Wonder: Too Many Times More?	 (10 minutes); Activity 1: A New Kind of Diagram (15 minutes); Activity 2:  Who Read More?	 (20 minutes); Cool-down:  Represent Multiplicative Comparison	 (5 minutes)
Source-aligned Edulytics model: One group read 30 books and another read 60 times as many. What is the second total?
First-party Cool-down (not gated original): Write a comparison equation for 400 items and 3 times as many.
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It changes the unit, place value, or operation.
